660.skill_description: Counseling sessions are the main body of cognitive behavioral therapy; through structured sessions, cognition and behavior are changed to solve problems. Progressing stepwise from automatic thoughts to intermediate beliefs to core beliefs, each session contains three parts: beginning, middle, and end.

661.skill_description: The opening part aims to set the tone and improve the efficiency of this session; usually it proceeds in order with mood assessment, obtaining the latest information, reviewing homework, and setting the agenda, so that the discussion focuses on the most important and processable topics.

662.skill_description: Assessing the client's current emotional state to grasp problem severity and improvement trends. Commonly using depression/Anxiety scales for weekly assessment, other emotions or overall mood can use a 0-100 emotion scale, as the basis for efficacy monitoring.

663.skill_description: Learn about the key events and changes since the last session. Encourage talking about the negative as well as attending to positive experiences; avoid getting into details, only an outline is needed, and when necessary include matters in the agenda to be handled in the middle segment.

664.skill_description: Jointly check with the client the completion of the homework assigned last time. This can strengthen the motivation to carry it out, present progress, and discover from the homework difficulties and clues worth discussion, including them in this agenda when necessary.

665.skill_description: Before formal discussion, jointly listing today's agenda items, clarifying priorities. The agenda can include issues the client cares about, counseling relationship and setting matters, and last session's unfinished topics, ensuring the session is focused and efficient.

666.skill_description: The middle part is the main body of the session; from the agenda select the most important topic for in-depth processing: first collect data, then conduct conceptualization and assessment; after completion, invite the client to record counseling notes and assign homework. Usually only 1-2 items can be processed.

667.skill_description: The ending part consolidates the gains and the alliance through session summary, homework, and session feedback. Summarize the key points and gains, confirm the willingness and obstacles for homework, and collect feelings and questions, adjusting the subsequent plan in time.

668.skill_description: Review the core content, insights, and gains of this discussion, clarify the key points that need to be recorded and the matters to be followed up. The summary can strengthen learning and memory, helping the client grasp the progress and paving the way for the homework.

669.skill_description: Before the end, clarify and confirm the homework, explain the goals and operating methods, and assess the willingness to complete and possible obstacles. When necessary adjust the difficulty or make it optional, because homework execution is closely related to treatment efficacy.

670.skill_description: Inviting the client to give feedback on this session's gains, feelings, and confusions, including important gains, homework feasibility, uncomfortable points, and unresolved issues. Handling negative experiences promptly, maintaining the counseling relationship, and planning next session's agenda.

536.skill_description: Automatic thoughts are thoughts that automatically arise in specific situations, directly affecting emotions, behaviors, and physiology. The core task of this stage is identifying and evaluating thinking; the end marker is the client's obvious emotional improvement, ability to handle situations effectively, and having learned to identify and evaluate Automatic thoughts.

537.skill_description: First identifying prominent emotions, then probing the Automatic thoughts at the time; can use Questioning, situation reenactment, prompts, or rational analysis to locate situations, thoughts, and feelings, and distinguish emotions from thoughts, laying the foundation for subsequent assessment and cognitive Intervention.

538.skill_description: In each agenda item, use a 0-100% scale to quantify emotion intensity and degree of belief in automatic thoughts; compare before and after to test session effectiveness, and adjust intervention strategies and homework arrangements accordingly, tracking treatment progress in a data-based way.

539.skill_name: Consolidation and application of the automatic-thoughts phase
539.skill_description: Record and consolidate the new thoughts and new behaviors; make counseling notes or coping cards, and practice and apply them repeatedly according to life situations; through homework, transfer the session gains into daily life to enhance self-help ability and maintain treatment effects.

540.skill_name: Learning to identify and evaluate Automatic thoughts
540.skill_description: Through systematic Homework practice, first learning to identify Automatic thoughts, then learning evaluation and correction; forming skills with standardized tools and steps, enabling the client to independently cope with future problems and maintain long-term mental health.

541.skill_description: The three-column table records date and time, situations, Automatic thoughts, and emotions, and rates belief and emotional intensity; used to capture and practice identifying Automatic thoughts in daily life, it is the foundational Homework tool of the Learning stage.

542.skill_description: On the basis of the monitoring form, add 'appropriate response' and 'conclusion', use 6 standard questions to evaluate the effectiveness and usefulness of thoughts, record changes in beliefs and emotions and the behavior to be taken, and promote the consolidation of cognition and behavior.

543.skill_description: In cognitive behavioral therapy, use the shaping technique to examine and revise automatic thoughts, integrate the evidence to form alternative thoughts, and at the same time assess the degree of belief and the emotional intensity, so as to relieve negative emotions and promote behavioral change.

544.skill_description: Borrowing the trial framework, simultaneously collect evidence supporting the automatic thought and opposing viewpoints, sort out the evidence through four typical questions, and integrate positive and negative information to derive a more reasonable alternative thought, correcting cognitive distortions such as overgeneralization.

545.skill_description: Facing ambiguous situations, helping the client propose multiple possible interpretations, finding evidence for each interpretation and estimating probabilities, then verifying through actions like re-contacting or calling with a different number, thereby alleviating Anxiety and suspicion, expanding the cognitive perspective.

546.skill_description: For events not yet occurred, building the range of outcomes from worst to best, assessing the most likely outcome, and preparing responses for the worst case and planning actions for the ideal outcome; correcting negative Anticipation about the future through weighing evidence, reducing Anxiety and depression.

547.skill_description: When evidence is insufficient, first changing behavior to change cognition, designing low-risk experimental situations, recording actual results and the degree of belief in old and new beliefs, testing and correcting views with behavioral results; also used to encourage trying new behaviors, consolidating alternative thoughts and functional habits.

548.skill_description: Borrowing from economics, comparing the benefits and costs of sticking with old ideas versus adopting alternative thoughts, motivating the choice of more advantageous views and implementing corresponding actions; also used for Working through resistance, clarifying the risks, costs, and benefits of changing and not changing.

549.skill_description: This chapter focuses on improving emotions with cognitive and behavioral methods, not yet listing Emotion techniques separately. The assessment stage often combines emotion naming and intensity rating, combining alternative thoughts and Behavioral experiments to alleviate emotional reactions like Anxiety and depression.

550.skill_description: The reference text mentions focusing attention on the answering task in examination situations and reducing rumination on threatening thoughts. Such attention management can be combined with cost-benefit analysis and behavioral experiments to help stabilize current performance and indirectly correct cognition.

551.skill_description: The text repeatedly emphasizes verifying hypotheses by taking concrete actions and making checklists and steps to improve the situation, embodying a problem-solving approach. This technique usually turns alternative thoughts into executable plans, implemented step by step with effects evaluated.

693.skill_description: Intermediate beliefs are located between automatic thoughts and core beliefs, embodied as psychological strategies of attitudes, assumptions, and rules. The counseling goal is to correct the compensation strategies, transforming them into flexible coping strategies, and through verification and practice form new behavioral modes and habits.

694.skill_description: This sub-stage, through identifying the composition of Intermediate beliefs, conducts psychoeducation and evaluates pros and cons, prompting the client to understand the testability and modifiability of their assumptions, laying the foundation for subsequent assessment, distilling new beliefs, and behavioral change.

695.skill_description: Following four identification steps: defining problem areas/life aspects; Clarify core beliefs through downward arrow; distilling attitudes and rules from Automatic thoughts; proposing and clarifying positive and negative hypotheses, to obtain testable Intermediate beliefs statements.

696.skill_description: Explain to the client the structure and logic of intermediate beliefs (attitude - assumption - rule), explain that compensatory strategies fail as situations change, that assumptions can be verified, and emphasize their learned nature and modifiability, enhancing the sense of feasibility of change.

697.skill_description: Using pros-and-cons analysis to focus on negative hypotheses, separately comparing past and present benefits and costs, highlighting that old strategies do more harm than good in the current situation, thereby strengthening the intrinsic motivation to revise hypotheses and try new behaviors.

698.skill_description: Use the 0-100% percentage scale to continuously record the degree of belief in the old / new beliefs, recommend daily tracking, so as to observe fluctuations and trends, monitor intervention effects, and guide the counseling process and goal adjustment.

699.skill_description: Testing the evidence and applicable boundaries of old hypotheses through Socratic Questioning and multiple cognitive techniques, distilling more adaptive alternative hypotheses, and accumulating supporting evidence to improve the credibility of new beliefs.

700.skill_description: Use heuristic questions to guide the client to examine assumptions from concrete examples, discover counterexamples and conditions, lower the certainty in old beliefs, and at the same time pave the way for forming new beliefs closer to the facts and with limiting conditions.

701.skill_description: On the basis of evidence, rewrite the old assumption into a new assumption of 'positive wording + limiting conditions', and evaluate the degree of belief in it; test and strengthen it with life examples and subsequent practice, making it more feasible and adaptive.

702.skill_description: For highest standards/perfectionism, setting a lower comparison benchmark (the evaluation zero point), guiding comparison against the zero point rather than the perfect point, immediately correcting the frustration from unreasonable comparison, promoting flexible, diverse evaluation.

703.skill_description: Use a continuous 0-100% scale to replace black-and-white thinking, construct more extreme scenarios for comparison and re-evaluation, so that the current situation obtains a more appropriate positioning in the continuum, reducing the catastrophic evaluation of 'It's awful'.

704.skill_description: Decompose the causes of an event into multiple factors and weight them by proportion, balancing internal and external attributions, clarifying the bias of 'all caused by me/them', and helping form an objective assessment of responsibility and more reasonable follow-up countermeasures.

705.skill_description: Breaking linear association into multiple stages, analyzing possible directions, conditions, and correction means link by link, discovering turning points and controllable points, alleviating chain catastrophizing or overly optimistic irrational Anticipation.

706.skill_description: Based on the 'immediate-Reinforcement short-circuit' model, bringing distant outcomes to the present through visualization/imagery, linking future consequences with current behaviors, thereby Undoing immediate Reinforcement, supporting reasonable choices.

707.skill_description: On the basis of the new belief, through behavioral experiments and behavioral rehearsal turn the cognitive change into behavioral change; first verify in small steps and accumulate evidence, then practice at high intensity, and finally solidify into a stable habit.

708.skill_description: Jointly design controllable, safe reality tests, compare the predictions and results of the old / new assumptions, gradually accumulate evidence to raise confidence in the new belief; applicable to the stage where confidence in the new belief is about 50-70%.

709.skill_description: On the basis of near-full belief (about 90%), requiring 'acting as if fully believing', realistically rehearsing new behavior scripts, Reinforcing new beliefs with experiential success and accelerating Habituation.

783.skill_description: The core-belief stage is the root-treating segment of cognitive behavioral therapy, carried out on the basis of work on automatic thoughts and intermediate beliefs, aiming to repair the negative core views of self, others, and the world, use present experience to correct the past, and promote cognitive selfhood, self-acceptance, and development.

784.skill_description: Identifying core beliefs is discovering the client's most general judgments about self, others, and the world. Can be directly extracted from Automatic thoughts, inductively summarizing common themes across situations, or using the downward arrow technique to drill down layer by layer to root beliefs.

785.skill_name: Identifying core beliefs from Automatic thoughts
785.skill_description: When the client reports situation-related Automatic thoughts, core beliefs are often revealed alongside. Focusing on sentence patterns with subjects like 'I/others/the world' and predicates as judgment sentences, such as 'I am incompetent' or 'the world is very cold'.

786.skill_name: Identifying core beliefs by inducing Automatic thoughts
786.skill_description: Collecting Automatic thoughts in multiple situations, comparing their common core and categorizing, such as repeatedly appearing ability, self-worth, or being-loved themes, thereby distilling the category of negative core beliefs like 'incapable' and 'unlovable'.

787.skill_name: Applying the downward arrow technique to identify core beliefs
787.skill_description: Using Questioning 'if this were true/happened, what would it mean?' to drill down layer by layer from surface thoughts, repeatedly probing their meaning and consequences, until reaching fundamental judgments about self, others, or the world, such as 'I am unlovable'.

788.skill_description: Evaluating core beliefs requires defining their themes and nature (self/others/world, positive/negative), identifying maintenance mechanisms (selective attention, denial, distortion), and combining the verification difficulty of the three belief levels, determining the order and timing of Intervention.

789.skill_description: Evaluation of core beliefs focuses on their origins and rationality judgments: combined with growth history data, examine significant others' expectations and evaluations, social comparison, traumatic experiences, and childhood interpretations and compensatory strategies, and scrutinize their evidence base.

790.skill_description: Through sorting out the individual's developmental history and interactions with significant others, trace back expectations and evaluations, social comparison, trauma, personal interpretations, and early behavioral styles, reconstruct the formation path, and locate the sources and maintaining factors of negative core beliefs.

791.skill_description: Guide a duel between the new and old beliefs, letting the new belief based on current positive experience dialogue and dialectically engage with the old negative belief, correcting early distorted interpretations, raising belief in 'capable/lovable' self-statements, and shaking the old schema.

792.skill_name: Application of the core-belief stage of counseling
792.skill_description: Apply the path of 'treating the symptoms first, then the root': first change automatic thoughts, work through intermediate beliefs, accumulate positive evidence in real problem-solving, and after sufficient confidence is reached, implement the new-old belief duel to replace negative core beliefs.
